name: Multiple Plant Polysaccharides
notes: can act on multiple plant polymers of hemicellulose, pectin, and cellulose

name: Cellulose-Associated
notes: β-Glucoside hydrolysis; may support cellulose-derived oligosaccharide utilization

name: Hemicellulose-Associated
notes: xylooligosaccharides and xyloglucan- or mannan-related oligosaccharides, potentially supporting hemicellulose-derived carbohydrate utilization.

name: Pectin-Associated
notes: pectic oligosaccharides, potentially supporting utilization of pectin breakdown products.

name: Starch/Glycogen Associated
notes: maltooligosaccharides and α-glucosides, potentially supporting utilization of starch- or glycogen-derived carbohydrates.

name: Chitin-Associated
notes: chitooligosaccharides and N-acetylhexosaminides, potentially supporting chitin-derived carbohydrate utilization. N-acetylhexosaminides may also originate from other glycoconjugates.

name: Other oligosaccharides
notes: Diverse glycoside and oligosaccharide transformations, including fructooligosaccharide utilization and oligosaccharide oxidation, that are not assigned to a single major polymer-associated group.

name: Cellobiose
notes: Glucose disaccharide produced during cellulose breakdown; utilization does not imply direct cellulose degradation.

name: Maltose
notes: Glucose disaccharide associated with starch and glycogen breakdown.

name: Sucrose
notes: Glucose–fructose disaccharide commonly found in plants; important for carbon transport and storage.

name: Trehalose
notes: Glucose disaccharide used for carbon storage and stress protection in many organisms.

name: Lactose
notes: Galactose–glucose disaccharide; utilization indicates potential to process lactose or related β-galactosides.

name: Mannobiose or Mannose (mixed size)
notes: Mannose-containing carbohydrates associated with mannan and other glycans; calls may represent monosaccharide or disaccharide processing.

name: Glucose
notes: Central hexose used in carbohydrate metabolism.

name: Xylose
notes: Pentose commonly derived from xylan and other plant polysaccharides.

name: Arabinose
notes: Pentose commonly found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including hemicellulose (e.g., arabinoxylan), arabinan, and pectin.

name: Mannose
notes: Hexose commonly found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including hemicellulose and pectin, as well as diverse glycoconjugates

name: Galactose
notes: Hexose found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including pectin (galactans) and some hemicelluloses, as well as other glycans.

name: Fructose
notes: Hexose found in sucrose and fructans (e.g., inulin and levan), as well as other carbohydrates.

name: Rhamnose
notes: Deoxyhexose commonly found in pectin (rhamnogalacturonans) and microbial polysaccharides.

name: N-Acetylglucosamine (Glc-NAc)
notes: Amino sugar found in chitin (fungal cell walls), bacterial peptidoglycan, and other glycoconjugates.

name: Succinate
notes: Succinate production via fumarate reductase ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü catalytic subunits frdA/frdB (K00244, K00245) plus membrane anchor subunits frdC/frdD (K00246, K00247). Note fumarate reductase is also involved in other metabolisms beyond succinate production; interpret in context of broader fermentative metabolism.

name: Butanol
notes: Butanol production via ABE fermentation pathway; requires butyryl-CoA formation (thiolase K00634 plus butyryl-CoA acetyltransferase K00929 or K01896) followed by reduction to butanol via butanol dehydrogenase (bdh; K00100) or NADH-dependent butanol dehydrogenase (K00544). Butyryl-CoA intermediate shared with butyrate pathway. Found predominantly in Clostridia.

name: Ethylene-Glycol-Degradation
notes: Ethylene glycol degradation via glycolate oxidase (K11472) or diol dehydratase (K18394) for initial oxidation, followed by alcohol dehydrogenase (K00001, K00121) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (K14085, K00128, K00149). Ethylene glycol is used as antifreeze in pipelines and gas processing facilities. Note: K11472 and K18394 removed per curation.

name: DNRA NrfA only, NO2 To NH4
Iron Oxidation
notes: Ferrous iron oxidation for energy conservation. Cyc2 (outer membrane cytochrome, broad iron oxidizers; Fe@Cyc2), MtoAB (neutrophilic iron oxidizers; Fe@MtoA & Fe@MtoB), FoxEYZ (acidophilic iron oxidizers; Fe@FoxE & Fe@FoxY & Fe@FoxZ), PioA (photoferrotrophic iron oxidation; Fe@PioA). HMMs from FeGenie database.

name: Iron/Manganese/Selenium-Reduction
notes: Dissimilatory Fe(III), Mn(IV), and potentially Se(VI) reduction via extracellular electron transfer (EET) systems, including MtrCAB in Shewanella (Fe@MtrA, Fe@MtrB_TIGR03509, Fe@MtrC_TIGR03507), Omc cytochromes in Geobacter (Fe@OmcS, Fe@OmcZ, Fe@OmcF), and ExtABCD in other iron reducers. These systems are not substrate-specific markers, so their presence does not distinguish Fe(III), Mn(IV), or Se(VI) reduction. HMMs from the DRAM Fe@ database

name: Arsenate Reduction
notes: ArrAB-mediated dissimilatory arsenate reduction using As(V) as a terminal electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration

name: Selenate Reduction
notes: SrdABC-mediated dissimilatory selenate reduction using Se(VI) as a terminal electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration

name: Possible Selenate or Chlorate Reduction
notes: Selenate/chlorate reductase (SerABC/ClrABC; K17050, K17051, K17052) — cannot distinguish selenate from chlorate reduction based on these KOs alone

name: Hydrogenotrophic
notes: For a few genome to encode potential to oxidize carbon monoxide, it must encode either the aerobic or anaerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase and it anaerobic, NOT be an acetogen/use the Wood Ljungdahl pathway

name: Acetoclastic
notes: For a genome to have hydrogneotrophic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA, at least 4 genes of the methyl branch of the Wood-lungdahl pathway,  part of the MTR complex, and at least one gene for any known hydrgenotrophic hdyrogenase.

name: Methylotrophic
notes: For a genome to have acetoclastic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA, part of the ACS_CODH complex, and either Acetate Kinase and Phosphotransacetylase OR Acetyl CoA Synthetase. There is a MANDATORY taxonomic requirement for this rule to run, and a MAG or genome must also belong to the genus Methanosarcina or the family Methanotrichaceae

name: Aerobic Methanotroph
notes: For a genome to have methyltotrophic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA and at least one substrate-demethylating corrinoid-dependent methyltransferase homolog "MtxB"

name: Methanogen Or ANME
notes: A genome that encodes adenylysulfate reductase and dissimilatory sulfite reductase

It must also encode any genes for denitrifcation narG, napA, nirK, nirS, norB

name: Fermentative-H2-(Fefe)
notes: FeFe hydrogenases; primarily fermentative H2 production across all subgroups. Group A is the most common fermentative H2-producing hydrogenase; Group B is electron-bifurcating; Group C is putatively sensory; Groups E and F are found in anaerobic fungi and diverse anaerobes. All subgroups associated with anaerobic fermentative metabolism.

name: H2-Metabolism-Nife-Group-1
notes: NiFe group 1 hydrogenases; membrane-bound, predominantly H2 uptake linked to respiratory electron transport chain. Most characterized members are H2-consuming; functional inference for uncharacterized members is based on phylogeny. Key for cathodic depolarization MIC and energy conservation in H2-rich systems including underground hydrogen storage.

name: H2-Metabolism-Nife-Group-2
notes: NiFe group 2 hydrogenases; putative sensory/regulatory function detecting environmental H2 concentrations and regulating expression of other hydrogenases. Do not contribute directly to energy conservation. Functional characterization is limited relative to other NiFe groups.

name: H2-Metabolism-Nife-Group-3
notes: Cytoplasmic bidirectional NiFe hydrogenases capable of both H2 production and consumption depending on prevailing redox conditions. Involved in NADH and ferredoxin redox balancing during fermentation and anaerobic metabolism. The bidirectional nature means functional direction cannot be inferred from gene presence alone and is condition-dependent.

name: H2-Metabolism-Nife-Group-4
notes: Membrane-bound energy-conserving NiFe hydrogenases primarily involved in H2 evolution, coupled to ion pumping for energy conservation under anaerobic conditions. Found in strict anaerobes, acetogens, and methanogens. Relevant in anaerobic digesters, shale systems, and underground hydrogen storage where H2 production by microbial communities affects system chemistry and storage integrity.

name: Eps-Production
notes: Exopolysaccharide biosynthesis and biofilm matrix structural genes including alginate biosynthesis (alg genes; K16566, K16557, K16556, K16555), Psl polysaccharide biosynthesis (K19290-K19296), PGA/ICA poly-GlcNAc synthesis (pgaABCD/icaABCD; K11936, K11937), and additional EPS biosynthesis genes. Any single gene indicates EPS production capacity. Drives pipeline fouling and MIC in engineered systems.

name: Quorum-Sensing
notes: Quorum sensing via three systems: (1) AHL/LuxI-LuxR: LuxI-type AHL synthases lasI (K13060) or rhlI/cepI/tofI homologs (K13061) paired with LuxR-type receptors lasR (K18304) or rhlR homologs (K18099) ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü both synthase and receptor required; (2) AI-2/LuxS system: LuxS S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase (K07173) ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü widely conserved but interpret alone cautiously as it has metabolic roles beyond QS; (3) AI-2 import via Lsr ABC transporter: LsrB substrate-binding (K10555), LsrC permease (K10556), LsrD permease (K10557), LsrA ATPase (K10558) ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü at least 2 subunits required ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü indicates active AI-2 uptake and response capacity.

name: Motility
notes: Flagellar motor (MotA K02410 or MotB K02411; at least one required) plus at least 3 structural/assembly genes from the flagellar complex. Required for surface approach and early biofilm attachment. Also relevant for chemotaxis toward carbon/electron donor sources in engineered systems.

name: Ion Homeostasis: K+ Uptake and Na+ Exclusion
notes: Halophilic salt-in osmoadaptation via K+ accumulation and Na+ exclusion. KdpABC P-type ATPase (K01546-K01548) imports K+; KdpDE (K07646, K07667) sensor-regulator. Mrp/Mnh Na+:H+ antiporter (K05565-K05571; Mrp subunit K05565 required plus at least 3 others). PhaABCDEFG K+ transporter (K05559-K05564; at least 2 of 6). TrkA/TrkH constitutive K+ uptake (K03499 & K03498; both required). NhaC Na+:H+ antiporter (K03315 or K07084). Highly relevant in hypersaline produced waters (TDS >200 g/L).

name: Compatible-Solutes: Glycine Betaine Synthesis
notes: Glycine betaine biosynthesis via two routes: (1) choline oxidation pathway ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü choline dehydrogenase (betA; K00108 or K11440) AND betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase (betB; K00130); or (2) sequential N-methylation of glycine ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü glycine/sarcosine methyltransferase (K18896) AND sarcosine/dimethylglycine methyltransferase (K18897).

name: Compatible-Solutes: Ectoine Synthesis
notes: Ectoine biosynthesis via complete ectABC pathway: diaminobutyrate acetyltransferase (ectA; K06718), diaminobutyrate aminotransferase (ectB; K00836), ectoine synthase (ectC; K06720) ‚Äö√Ñ√∂‚àö√ë‚àö√Ü all three required. Ectoine hydroxylase (ectD; K10674) additionally produces hydroxyectoine with enhanced thermostability. Major compatible solute in halophilic bacteria.

name: Compatible-Solutes: Sugar Derived Synthesis
notes: Biosynthesis of sugar-derived compatible solutes. Trehalose: OtsAB (K00697 & K01087; both required), TreYZ (K06044 or K01236), TreS (K05343), TreP (K05342). Mannosylglycerate: mpgSP (K05947). Mannitol: mtlD (K00009). Note K05342 and K05343 overlap with Trehalose Use row in Carbon Degradation.

name: Compatible-Solutes: Methylated Transport
notes: Transport of glycine betaine, choline, proline, and related methylated osmoprotectants. BetP/T/S BCCT transporter (K02168), carnitine/betaine antiporter (K05245), OpuD betaine transporter (K05020). ProVWX ABC transporter (K02000 & K02001 & K02002; all three required). OpuABC (K05845, K05846, K05847; at least 2 subunits). Glutamine ABC (K10036, K10037, K10038; at least 2 subunits). ProP MFS transporter (K03762); ProQ effector (K03607).

name: Compatible-Solutes: Ectoine Transport
notes: Ectoine/hydroxyectoine uptake via EhuABC ABC transporter (EhuA ATPase K02028, EhuC/D permease K02029, EhuB substrate-binding protein K02030). At least 2 of 3 subunits required for metagenomic data. Organisms with transport but not synthesis genes are ectoine scavengers.

name: Aldehyde-Resistance
notes: Resistance to aldehyde biocides (e.g., glutaraldehyde, formaldehyde) mediated by aldehyde oxidoreductases and aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases (K00149, K14085), which detoxify reactive aldehyde compounds.

name: Qac-Resistance
notes: Resistance to quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) disinfectants mediated by multidrug efflux transporters (K08167, K11741) that export toxic biocides from the cell.

name: Biocide-Efflux-(General)
notes: Broad-spectrum efflux genes for biocide and multidrug resistance. MexA/membrane fusion protein (K03585), MATE efflux (K03400), MexB/RND pump (K18138), AcrD/RND pump (K18324), AcrF/RND pump (K18142), and SMR family pumps: Mmr (K03297), EbrA/EbrB paired SMR pump (K11814 & K11815), Ebr SMR pump (K18975). Aldehyde dehydrogenase (K14085) provides chemical detoxification capacity. RND pumps (2.A.6 TCDB family) provide broad substrate efflux relevant in oil and gas and wastewater systems. General row is superset of Aldehyde Resistance sub-row.
